advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the source head has no non-identity commit headers (encoding/gpgsig/mergetag), or preserve them when re-creating the head, since commit-tree drops them and the tree-equality assertion cannot detect the loss.
evidence: infra/scripts/reclaim_bridge_history.py:204: `for line in headers.splitlines():` only branches on `author `/`committer `/`parent `, discarding any other header line
infra/scripts/reclaim_bridge_history.py:261: `command = ["git", "-C", str(repo), "commit-tree", tree]` reconstructs the commit from tree/parents/identity/message only
infra/scripts/reclaim_bridge_history.py:306: the only head-level check compares `{rewritten}^{tree}` to source_tree, so a changed/dropped commit header on the head is not caught
advisory.finding: restore_current_bridge_state re-creates the rewritten head with `git commit-tree`, which only preserves tree, parents, author/committer identities, and message extracted by _commit_metadata; any other head-commit headers (e.g. `encoding`, `gpgsig`, `mergetag`, or custom headers) are silently dropped, and the head-tree equality assertion cannot detect the loss because it compares only trees, not commit headers.

Ticket AC (6d50-8449-e71a-45b4) 'A completed dry run leaves the source remote tickets ref unchanged' and comment 'retaining exact movement detection for each' — the movement-DETECTION branch has no positive test
ABSENCE: no test in tests/integration/test_reclaim_bridge_history.py updates refs/heads/tickets or the protected tag on the remote mid-run and asserts a nonzero exit / 'changed during dry run' stderr
advisory.finding: The protected-ref immutability guard's positive-detection branch is untested: no test asserts the dry run FAILS when the source `tickets` ref or the protected tag actually moves during the run. `main` snapshots refs before the rewrite and re-checks `if protected_remote_refs(...) != old_refs: raise ReclaimError('source tickets ref or protected tag changed during dry run')`, but the only test that exercises `protected_remote_refs` change-detection (test_unrelated_remote_ref_movement_does_not_fail_dry_run) moves an UNRELATED ref and asserts SUCCESS. A regression that neuters the comparison (e.g. always-equal, or omitting the final re-snapshot) would pass all six integration tests.
scenarios: Another writer moves the source tickets ref between the pre- and post-snapshot during a real rehearsal; the guard must abort but a regression silently reports DRY RUN SUCCESS.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a wrapper-based test mirroring test_unrelated_remote_ref_movement, but on the 2nd `ls-remote origin` call run `update-ref refs/heads/tickets <other-tip>` (or move the protected tag); assert `completed.returncode != 0` and 'changed during dry run' in `completed.stderr`.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Drain importer stdout/stderr and exporter stderr concurrently (e.g. threads or communicate) rather than reading them only after importer.wait()/the filter loop, to avoid a pipe-buffer deadlock.
evidence: infra/scripts/reclaim_bridge_history.py:185: `exporter_stderr = exporter.stderr.read()` runs only after the filter loop, so exporter stderr accumulates while the filter is blocked
`--quiet` is passed to fast-import (line 173) which bounds its output, and the ticket records a successful 64k-commit live rehearsal — an ABSENCE-of-observed-failure mitigation, not a guarantee
dropped.finding: export_and_import calls importer.wait() before reading importer.stdout/importer.stderr, and reads exporter.stderr only after the full filter loop completes; if fast-import (or fast-export progress) writes more than the OS pipe buffer to a pipe that is not concurrently drained, the process can deadlock.
